J. Manges Cabin / James or Jimmy Manges Cabin near Cottonwood Creek

source_backed_facts.fact: The current ranger station is the relocated Lee Mangus/Manges homestead cabin; HABS identifies it as survey WY-108 and the National Park Service identifies it as today's Jenny Lake Ranger Station.
The NPS dates the homestead cabin to 1925, while HABS describes it as built before July 1929. Preserve this date discrepancy in provenance.
The cabin was acquired and moved to South Jenny Lake in 1930 for use as the park's museum and visitor facility; it later became the ranger station.
HABS records a room added at the east end in 1937, probably with Civilian Conservation Corps labor.
HABS sheet 2 dimensions the wall envelope at 20 feet 6 inches by 36 feet 9 inches.
HABS sheet 3 dimensions the peak at 18 feet above floor line and the ceiling line at 7 feet 9 inches.
The HABS material list specifies a stone foundation, saddle-jointed log walls, and a wood-shingle roof.
The west entrance elevation has a supported porch canopy, a vertical-plank door, a multi-light window, and a decorative diagonal-log king-post treatment in the gable.
The north long elevation documents three multi-light windows; the other elevations document their own asymmetric door and window arrangements.
The building remains a working ranger station beneath a wooded South Jenny Lake canopy, distinct from the nearby Crandall Studio visitor center.
